transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Samir Desai (Redwood SE), Laura Mitchell (CISO, Pioneer), Rajiv Kapoor (Head of Infra, Pioneer), Maya Ortiz (Legal, Pioneer), Ethan Wu (Platform Eng, Pioneer)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
High-level security review focused on encryption at rest and in transit, customer-managed keys (BYOK), HSM-backed key stores, key import/export constraints, audit logging for key usage, and data residency requirements. Pioneer has strict regulatory needs and want BYOK with HSM assurances; discussed envelope encryption, key wrapping, rotation, access controls and integration points with Redwood Private and Dedicated.

Topics: encryption at rest, in transit (TLS), KMS options, BYOK import, HSM vs software KMS, envelope encryption, audit logs, key rotation, SSO/RBAC ties, data residency, SOC2/ISO artifacts.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes. quick round robin?
[00:10] Laura Mitchell: hi yeah Laura here, CISO at Pioneer. we put this on to understand how Redwood handles keys and encryption, byok requirements and whether we can get HSM backed keys.
[00:18] Rajiv Kapoor: Rajiv, head of infra. major constraints: no plaintext sensitive data leaving our VPC, we need auditability and key separation, and certs for FIPS 140-2 where possible.
[00:26] Maya Ortiz: Maya from legal, want to flag export control and key escrow questions up front.
[00:30] Alex Chen: great, thanks. Priya and Samir from our SE team will cover the technical details. 
[00:35] Priya Sharma: hi! quick agenda — encryption in transit, at rest, customer-managed keys (BYOK), HSM options, rotation, audit logs, and next steps/PoC. is that right?
[00:43] Laura: yep. also want to confirm what Redwood stores vs what stays in Pioneer infra.

[02:12] Priya: ok encryption in transit first — we use TLS 1.2/1.3 on all endpoints, strong ciphers, mutual TLS option for our private deployments, and we can support VPC peering or private endpoints so traffic doesn't traverse public internet. sometimes transcripts say mtls, we mean mTLS.
[03:05] Ethan Wu: if traffic is private endpoint only, will Redwood ever terminate TLS outside our network?
[03:12] Samir: for Redwood Private deployments you run the control plane or we provide a customer-managed control plane; in either case you can choose that the TLS termination happens inside your VPC. for hosted mode termination is in our infra but we offer dedicated zones.
[04:00] Rajiv: ok good. next, at rest — what gets encrypted and where are the keys?
[04:10] Priya: primary data at rest is the model cache, request logs, KV caches and persistent storage for customer artifacts. by default we use our managed KMS with envelope encryption, where data keys are generated and wrapped by a root key. for customers with BYOK we support importing keys or connecting to their KMS via external key references.
[05:02] Laura: clarify import vs external key reference?
[05:10] Priya: import means you generate a key in your HSM and import the wrapped key material into our managed key store under strict import rules; external key reference (aka key-referencing) keeps keys in your KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KV) and we call it via API — we do not hold the unwrapped key material. both approaches have tradeoffs.
[06:15] Rajiv: we need HSM-backed keys, and we prefer keys to never be exported from our HSM. which option ensures that?
[06:24] Samir: if you want keys to never leave your HSM then key-referencing (external KMS) is the safer path; Redwood will call your KMS to perform wrap/unwrap or sign operations. alternatively we support BYOK with import, but that requires you to export a wrapped key blob — some HSMs allow wrapped export under an export token — so you need to validate with your HSM vendor and policy.
[07:05] Laura: we'd prefer not to share key material — so external KMS integration. what's the latency and availability impact?
[07:12] Priya: there is a small RTT hit when we call your KMS per envelope unwrap, but we mitigate by using envelope encryption and caching unwrapped data keys in volatile memory with strict TTLs and access controls. cache TTLs are configurable and audited. for high-throughput we recommend a dedicated capacity plan to keep cache rates and concurrency within SLOs.
[08:03] Ethan: is the data key caching stored in RAM only? what about persistent swap?
[08:10] Samir: yes, memory-only, never written to disk; if host restarts cache is empty. for Private deployments we can further restrict to hardware-enforced memory protections.

[09:45] Rajiv: what about audit logs for key operations — we need to show when keys were used and by what principal.
[09:54] Priya: we emit KMS usage logs and key operation events to our audit pipeline and can forward logs to your SIEM or to an S3-like endpoint in your account. we also generate per-request trace metadata (request id, model id, user id, key id) that you can correlate. some minor transcription errors: key id shows sometimes as kid, but it's the key identifier.
[10:35] Laura: retention requirements — we need immutable audit trails for 7 years for compliance. can you support that?
[10:44] Alex: Redwood can forward logs to your account or to a third-party log archive; retention is up to you if we deliver to your bucket. we also keep an internal audit trail for access control, but retention there is subject to plan — for enterprise we can extend retention or ship logs to your storage.

[12:12] Maya: legal question — if we use BYOK with Redwood hosted, who is the key custodian? do we need escrow?
[12:20] Samir: with external key reference you remain custodian. with import into Redwood's HSM you can maintain control but Redwood operates the HSM — we provide attestations and HSM audit logs. if escrow is required we can discuss a key-splitting approach or using your on-prem HSM for ultimate custody via Private deployment.
[13:18] Maya: what about subpoenas or legal holds? we need to know Redwood's policy.
[13:26] Alex: we'll include our legal policy and SOC2/ISO artifacts in the doc pack. in hosted mode Redwood retains control for operational reasons, but we can do contractual commitments on access and attestations.

[15:00] Rajiv: technical: can Redwood support AWS CloudHSM or Azure Dedicated HSM for BYOK?
[15:08] Priya: yes, we have integrations with AWS KMS + CloudHSM and Azure Dedicated HSM via key referencing. for CloudHSM specifically the API patterns are slightly different but we support wrapping/unwrapping with the appropriate key material.
[16:05] Ethan: is there an example flow for envelope encryption? would be good to see sequence diagram.
[16:12] Samir: absolutely — typical flow: 1) client request hits Redwood, 2) application generates a data key (or Redwood requests a wrapped data key via your KMS), 3) data key decrypts payload in memory, 4) Redwood stores ciphertext and the wrapped data key, 5) on read Redwood unwraps data key via calling your KMS (if external) then decrypts. we'll send diagrams.
[17:30] Laura: what about rotating keys — can we force rotate and have Redwood re-wrap historic blobs?
[17:37] Priya: rotation patterns: you can rotate the master key in your KMS; we rewrap existing data key envelopes on read/write depending on your policy, or we can run a background rewrap job during a migration window. we log both the old and new key ids used. there is a performance hit for bulk rewrap.

[19:20] Rajiv: any support for split key / key splitting or multi-party HSM?
[19:28] Samir: we support integrating with HSMs that support key custodianship and split key schemes; Redwood itself does not do secret-sharing across our team for custody — we rely on the customer's HSM/manager capabilities for split control. in Private deployment we can support a model where you hold root keys and Redwood holds operational subkeys, with clear ACL boundaries.

[21:10] Maya: compliance certifications — do you have SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001?
[21:18] Alex: yes SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 in our enterprise pack. we'll attach certs. also FIPS validated module usage varies by deployment — we'll provide details for HSM vendors.

[22:45] Laura: data residency — if we need EU-only storage for backups and logs, can Redwood guarantee that?
[22:53] Priya: yes, with Dedicated or Private deployments you can pin regions and storage locations. for hosted customers we have region-specific deployments and can route traffic and store backups in specified regions. we'll need to capture which Pioneer data needs EU-residency.

[24:05] Ethan: curious about SSO and RBAC mapping to keys — can we map key usage to specific roles?
[24:12] Samir: we integrate with SAML/SSO and provision RBAC in our console. key permissions are tied to service roles and users; audit logs include principal identity. for deeper control, external KMS principals can be constrained by your own IAM policies.

[26:30] Rajiv: what about emergency key rotation/compromise scenarios — can Redwood perform rapid revocation and what are the steps?
[26:38] Priya: quick revocation path: disable key at the KMS (external) — this prevents unwrap; Redwood will return errors; we can also revoke active sessions and invalidate caches. you'll want a runbook for re-encrypting data if key is permanently compromised. we recommend a canary test and a staged rewrap.

[28:00] Laura: are there any limits on key types or algorithms? we need RSA/ECC/AEAD support.
[28:07] Samir: we support AES-GCM and AES-CTR with HMAC for payloads, and key-wrapping with RSA-OAEP or RSA-PSS and ECC where supported by the HSM. for model signatures we support signing with ECDSA. we'll provide a compatibility matrix.

[30:10] Priya: one subtle point: some transcription tools confuse KV cache with K-V cache or kv-cache — that's our in-memory tokenizer cache. important to understand that KV cache encryption is applied in flight and at rest.

[31:20] Ethan: can we get per-token logging for audit or is that too noisy?
[31:28] Alex: per-token logs are usually too high-volume; we do request-level traces which include token counts and hash digests for content fingerprinting without storing PII. you can enable additional telemetry but it's expensive and noisy.

[33:05] Rajiv: network controls for KMS calls — can Redwood call our KMS endpoints over a private link?
[33:12] Priya: yes we support VPC endpoints and private link integrations; the KMS calls can be routed through your network or via a private peering. for some cloud HSMs a dedicated HSM appliance requires VPN/privatelink. we'll map that in the architecture doc.

[35:00] Maya: contractually, what assurances do we get that Redwood employees cannot access our keys or plaintext?
[35:07] Samir: we have strict RBAC, least privilege, and privileged access reviews. for external KMS the unwrapped keys are only in your control; for imports to Redwood-managed HSMs we provide attestations, access logs, and separation of duties. we can add contract clauses for privileged access reviews and notification windows.

[36:42] Laura: any penetration testing around KMS flows?
[36:49] Alex: yes we run regular pentests and will include summary results in the pack; for enterprise we can enable joint testing or allow you to run tests in a sandbox deployment.

[38:30] Priya: quick note on HSM attestation: remote attestation and hardware-backed key proofs (attestation certificates) are supported for certain vendors; we'll include specifics per vendor (AWS CloudHSM attestation, Azure Dedicated HSM certs, etc).

[40:15] Rajiv: curious about cost implications — if we use external KMS calls per unwrap, will that blow cost?
[40:22] Alex: there is an additional call cost on the KMS side per unwrap; our recommend pattern is envelope keys + caching to minimize calls. for predictable workloads we also recommend Redwood Dedicated to control concurrency and cache hit rates — we'll share cost modeling examples.

[42:05] Ethan: ok good. on the PoC: we'd like to validate an external KMS flow with our AWS account and CloudHSM — test key unwrap times, cache behavior, and log forwarding.
[42:14] Priya: perfect, we'll provision a PoC plan and schedule a demo.

[44:00] Alex: recap — action items: send SOC2/ISO and whitepaper, share KMS/BYOK integration docs, schedule PoC week of Aug 17, Pioneer to provide network diagram. any other items?
[44:12] Laura: please include sample SLA language about KMS unavailability and fallback behaviour.
[44:20] Maya: also include export control / legal guidance.
[44:30] Alex: noted. thanks everyone.
[45:00] Meeting closed.

Notes about transcript quality: transcription occasionally mangled acronyms (HSM -> H-S-M, KMS -> K-M-S) and names; speaker tags were accurate for the most part but small overlaps/crosstalk present.
